    Module

    src/Connector.Infrastructure

    Layer infrastructure · project Connector.Infrastructure · Services: 2, Entities: 8, DbContexts: 1, Background services: 3, Hosted services: 3, Options: 5

    Project navigation: Connector.Infrastructure

    Overview 🤖

    Manages infrastructure components for the connector, including API key authentication, app setting encryption, audit logging, and dynamic export services.

    Responsibilities. Manages API key authentication, encrypts app settings, logs audit events, and handles dynamic export operations.

    AI draft from the facts on this page; review it, then write the module's documentation yourself.

    Key components

    Component Kind Used by Summary
    ExportLogDbContext dbcontext 67 EF Core DbContext for the export log (SQLite). Tables: ExportRun, AppSetting (key/value config store), AuditLog. Schema is managed via EF Core migrations in Connector.Infrastructure/Migrations/. Startup calls Database.MigrateAsync() — add new changes via dotnet ef migrations add.
    AuditService service 41 Writes non-fatal, append-only audit entries to the AuditLog table. Failures are logged as warnings and never propagate — audit must not interrupt business logic. Every detail is scrubbed of credentials (Scrub) before it is stored, whatever the caller put into it.
    AppSettingsStore class 32 Typed find/deserialize/upsert helpers over AppSettings: one place for the find-null-check-deserialize (read) and find-null-check-add-or-mutate-save (write) pattern.
    DynamicExportService service 18 Query/build engine behind the connector's export paths: the legacy single-mapping flat/nested-JSON pipeline (ExportMappingConfig, still served by /api/pipeline/* — see DynamicExportService.LegacyMapping.cs) and the ExportNode tree engine (Export Definitions 2.0 — see DynamicExportService.ExportNode.cs) side by side, plus the shared GDPR denylist (DynamicExportService.Gdpr.cs) and output-format writers (DynamicExportService.Output.cs) both paths use. Kept as one partial class split across files by responsibility, rather than separate classes, so every existing DynamicExportService.* call site across the API/Infrastructure/test projects keeps working unchanged. This file holds the members shared across every other part: the nesting-depth cap, the build-result shape, the connection fingerprint, and the dialect lookup both query engines build on.
    ErrorSanitizer class 17 Strips credentials from error text. Several endpoints return an exception's message to the caller (a "test connection"/preview action is only useful if it says why it failed), but Npgsql can echo the offending connection string — including the ERP password — back inside an exception message. Detail is the single choke point every such call site routes through, so the diagnostic value survives but a credential can't leak through it. ForLogging does the same for logged exceptions, and Scrub for any other text such as audit details.
    UserStore class 6 Lookup and seeding helpers over Users.
    ExportDefinitionEntity entity 4 One saved, independently named and scheduled export: a name, the table it's rooted at, its ExportNode tree, and the output format/schedule it runs with. Replaces the single AppSetting-backed mapping + presets (ExportMapping/ExportPresets).
    ExportDefinitionRunner class 4 The one execution path behind every trigger of an ExportDefinitionEntity — manual run/test (ExportDefinitionEndpoints) and scheduled runs (ExportDefinitionWorker) all call ExecuteAsync, so every run — scheduled or manual — writes exactly one ExportDefinitionRunEntity row, with identical Failed/error-message semantics regardless of trigger.

    Components

    ApiKeyStore

    class · ApiKeyStore.cs

    Machine-to-machine credential check for endpoints a "dedicated API user" calls directly (no interactive login) — e.g. an external system triggering a saved export preset. Deliberately not BCrypt: a BCrypt verify is intentionally slow (work-factor tuned to resist brute-forcing a human-chosen password) and this runs on every single request rather than once at login, while a generated API key is already high-entropy, so a fast, constant-time SHA-256 comparison is the appropriate trade-off here. Never stores or compares the raw key — only its hash, both at rest (config) and in memory.

    Linked tests: ApiKeyStoreTests.TryAuthenticate_MatchingKey_ReturnsTrueWithConfiguredName, ApiKeyStoreTests.TryAuthenticate_MultipleConfiguredKeys_MatchesTheRightOne, ApiKeyStoreTests.TryAuthenticate_NoConfiguredKeys_ReturnsFalse, ApiKeyStoreTests.TryAuthenticate_WrongKey_ReturnsFalse, ApiKeyStoreTests.Hash_SameInput_IsDeterministicAndLowercaseHex (via ApiKeyStore.Hash(string)) — test code that uses it, not coverage

    Member Summary Derived from code Complexity
    Hash(string) Hex-encoded SHA-256 of rawKey — what belongs in Auth:ApiKeys[].KeyHash config (generate with e.g. printf '%s' '<key>' | sha256sum). 1

    AppSettingEncryptionMigrator

    class · AppSettingEncryptionMigrator.cs

    One-time, idempotent startup step that encrypts every AppSetting.Value still stored as plaintext — rows written before EncryptedStringConverter existed. The converter only encrypts a row when it is saved again, and several keys (e.g. scheduler_config, read on every worker tick) are rarely re-saved, so without this they would stay plaintext on disk indefinitely and trigger the converter's plaintext warning on every single read.

    Linked tests: AppSettingEncryptionTests.Migrator_EncryptsPlaintextRows_LeavesCiphertextAlone_AndIsIdempotent (via AppSettingEncryptionMigrator.EncryptPlaintextRowsAsync(ExportLogDbContext, IDataProtectionProvider, ILogger, CancellationToken)) — test code that uses it, not coverage

    CronSchedule

    class · CronSchedule.cs

    Minimal 5-field cron matcher (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, UTC) for Schedule. Not a general cron library: no seconds field, no L/W/# extensions — only what the UI's Manual/Hourly/Daily/Weekly presets plus a free-text advanced field can produce. The matching logic is a few dozen lines, so no scheduling library is used.

    ConnectionFingerprint(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig) Identifies which system a connection points at — host, port, and database — deliberately excluding Username/Password so a pure credential rotation against the same logical target (a password change, a different service account for the same database) never counts as a target change. Used to pin the connection an import run was staged against and verify it still matches at release (StagedConnectionFingerprint, ReleaseAsync). 1
    ExecuteExportNodeQueryAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.IDataSourceProvider, Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig, string, Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNode, System.Threading.CancellationToken, int?, System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlySet<string>?, Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportRecordSelection?) ⚠ Runs one ExportNode tree (rooted at rootTable) and returns one JSON tree per root row — the generic successor to ExecuteNestedJsonQueryAsync that also covers plain scalar columns, so it is the only query path BuildExportNodeAsync needs regardless of output format. The database returns plain rows, one query per tree node; the tree is assembled in C# (ExecuteTreeQueryAsync). Every scalar is a JSON string of its ::text form (or JSON null), an array node with no matches is [], an object node with no match is null, and an object node with several matches fails the export. GDPR enforcement is two layers: a denylisted SourceField is excluded from the SELECT list entirely (so it never leaves the database, and — since this is re-evaluated against the current denylist on every run — a definition saved before a field was denylisted is covered too, not just newly-saved ones), plus StripGdprFieldsRecursive's output-key match as a second, independent layer of defence-in-depth. dependencies: none; side effects (inferred): db 6
    ExecuteQueryAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.IDataSourceProvider, Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig, Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportMappingConfig, System.Threading.CancellationToken, int?, System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlySet<string>?) Flat query behind the legacy single-mapping export (CSV/Excel/flat JSON) and its preview: one row per source-table row, enabled fields as columns and each enabled relation flattened into a delimited string via a correlated string-aggregate subquery. GDPR-denied fields are left out of the SELECT and stripped again from the results; NULLs come back as "". dependencies: ISqlDialect, IDataSourceProvider, QueryResult, NativeSqlQuery; side effects (inferred): db 15
    BuildImportEnvelopeBytes(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList<System.Text.Json.Nodes.JsonObject>, string, System.DateTimeOffset, Connector.Infrastructure.ExportProvenance?) Writes records as an ImportEnvelope for another connector instance: schemaVersion (SupportedSchemaVersion), definition (the receiving instance's import definition, which routes the file), generatedAt, the optional advisory provenance, and records. 2
    ApplyExportNodeMappingsRecursive(System.Text.Json.Nodes.JsonObject, Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNode) Walks a parsed row tree in lockstep with the ExportNode tree that produced it, applying each scalar field's FieldMapping (transform/default/data-type coercion) at the point the value is read — deliberately in C#, not SQL: a malformed single row's value (e.g. non-numeric text under a Number field) degrades to a best-effort string instead of aborting the whole query the way a SQL-side numeric cast failure would. Called by ExecuteExportNodeQueryAsync on every fetched row; public (like this class's other pure C# post-processing, e.g. BuildCsvBytes) so transform behavior is unit-testable against a hand-built tree without a live Postgres connection. 5
    BuildExcelBytes(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList<System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary<string, string>>, System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList<string>, string, System.DateTimeOffset) Writes flat records to a one-sheet .xlsx workbook: a metadata row (schema version, extraction time), a header row, then one row per record.     EncryptedStringConverter

    class · EncryptedStringConverter.cs

    Encrypts a string column at rest via ASP.NET Core Data Protection. Applied to Value, which stores the ERP connection config including its password, so a stolen backup or disk snapshot of the SQLite file doesn't expose it. EF Core runs the conversion on every SaveChanges/materialization, so every caller — AppSettingsStore's helpers and the several call sites that read AppSettings directly — keeps seeing plaintext JSON; only the bytes actually persisted to disk are ciphertext.

    ErrorSanitizer

    class · ErrorSanitizer.cs

    Strips credentials from error text. Several endpoints return an exception's message to the caller (a "test connection"/preview action is only useful if it says why it failed), but Npgsql can echo the offending connection string — including the ERP password — back inside an exception message. Detail is the single choke point every such call site routes through, so the diagnostic value survives but a credential can't leak through it. ForLogging does the same for logged exceptions, and Scrub for any other text such as audit details.

    ReleaseAsync(Connector.Infrastructure.ExportLogDbContext, Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunEntity, string, string, Connector.Infrastructure.AuditService, Connector.Core.DataSources.IDataSourceProviderResolver, System.Threading.CancellationToken) Applies run's persisted PlanJson to the ERP: one conditional UPDATE per row — every column that row's plan changes, guarded by every one of that row's captured expected-old-values in a single WHERE clause, so a row commits all its changed columns or none of them, never half. Zero affected rows means the row's ERP state moved on since staging; that row is excluded, counted in ConflictCount, and left untouched — it does not fail the run. An unrelated failure (a thrown exception — e.g. a constraint violation) rolls back everything committed so far in this call and marks the run Failed, matching the "no silent partial success" rule already enforced on the export side.     ImportWorker

    class · ImportWorker.cs

    A sibling of ExportWorker that polls an inbound/ staging folder instead of writing to one. Every vendor-supplied file dropped there is manifest-checked, idempotency-checked against (ImportDefinitionId, Sha256Checksum), walked by ImportNodeWalker against the ImportEnvelope — the definition field says which saved ImportDefinitionEntity to use — and staged as an ImportRunEntity at PendingReview, with ImportDefinitionEntity frozen onto it as DefinitionSnapshotJson. This worker never writes to the ERP itself — that's ImportRunReleaser's job, once a human approves the staged plan.

    SessionRevocationStore

    class · SessionRevocationStore.cs

    JWT revocation: stores, per username, the earliest a JWT for that user may have been issued to still be considered valid. Every token carries its own issued-at claim (see AuthEndpoints), and Program.cs's OnTokenValidated handler rejects any token issued before that cutover. Backed by the encrypted-at-rest AppSettingEntity key/value store rather than a dedicated table. Self-service only: a user can revoke their own sessions (POST /api/auth/revoke-my-sessions). There is no admin action to revoke another user's sessions, since there is no role model to authorize it.
